cards.html:
GitHub Actions runs workflows: YAML files in .github/workflows/. When an event happens (a push, a pull request, a schedule), GitHub starts a fresh virtual machine, a runner, and executes the jobs you defined. Figure 9 shows the structure; here is the smallest useful workflow:

.github/workflows/ci.yml (Level 1 version):

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.3.3
      - run: uv sync --locked
      - run: uv run pytest

LineMeaning
name (1)Shown in the Actions tab and in PR checks.
on (3–6)The triggers: pushes to main, and every pull request (any branch). Other triggers: schedule (cron), workflow_dispatch (a manual button), release, workflow_call (reusable).
jobs (8)A map of jobs. Jobs run in parallel unless one says needs: other-job.
runs-on (10)The runner image. ubuntu-latest is the standard choice: fast to start and free for public repositories.
steps (11)Executed in order, in the same machine and directory. If a step fails (non-zero exit code), the job stops.
uses (12–13)Runs a ready-made action: owner/repo@version. checkout clones your repository into the runner; setup-uv installs uv and, if needed, Python.
run (14–15)Runs a shell command. Its exit code decides success: pytest returns 1 when a test fails, so the job turns red.
Concept: uses vs. run, and pinning versions

run executes your own command. uses executes someone else's code (an action), so pin it to a version. @v7 is a moving major tag that receives fixes; @v10.3.3 is an exact release. Some projects, like setup-uv, no longer publish major tags, so you must name an exact version. The most secure option is to pin the full commit SHA (Level 5). The versions in this book were current in November 2026; check each action's README for newer ones.

Interview tip: actions/setup-python

Most projects you will meet use actions/setup-python@v7 with python-version: "3.12" and then pip install -r requirements.txt. It works the same way; setup-uv simply does both jobs (Python and packages) and is faster.

cards.s: Five more things you need in almost every workflow
cards.html:
common step options:

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Show where we are            # 1. a readable name in the UI
        run: |                             # 2. several commands
          python --version
          echo "Triggered by $GITHUB_EVENT_NAME on $GITHUB_REF_NAME"
      - name: Train
        working-directory: ./training      # 3. run in a subfolder
        env:                               # 4. env vars for this step
          SAMPLE_FRAC: "0.1"
        run: uv run python train.py
      - name: Upload logs only if something failed
        if: failure()                      # 5. conditional step
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: training-logs
          path: training/logs/

cards.s: Five more things you need in almost every workflow
cards.html:
run: | is YAML for a multi-line string; each line is one shell command. GitHub sets many variables automatically (GITHUB_SHA, GITHUB_REF_NAME, GITHUB_EVENT_NAME, RUNNER_OS, …); the same values are available as expressions (${{ github.sha }}). A step with if: failure() runs only when an earlier step failed: ideal for collecting logs and reports that explain the failure. always() runs regardless; success() is the default.

What if… my workflow does not start at all?

What happens: You pushed, but the Actions tab shows nothing.

Why: Go through this checklist; it covers nearly every case:

  • The file is not in .github/workflows/ exactly (a typo such as

.github/workflow/ is silently ignored) or does not end in .yml/.yaml.

cards.s: Five more things you need in almost every workflow
cards.html:
• The YAML is invalid. The Actions tab then shows a failed run with an error like Invalid workflow file: … (Line: 12, Col: 9), but only if GitHub could find the file. Indentation with tabs is a common cause.
  • The trigger does not match: branches: [main] but you pushed to

feature/x; or paths-ignore matched every changed file.

  • The workflow file exists only on your branch: schedule and

workflow_dispatch use the file on the default branch, and the manual button only appears after the file is on main.

  • Actions are disabled in Settings → Actions → General, or the commit message contains [skip ci].

cards.s: Five more things you need in almost every workflow
cards.html:
What you do: Validate locally before pushing: actionlint (a linter for workflow files, also available as a pre-commit hook) catches syntax errors, unknown keys and many expression mistakes.

What if… my workflow runs twice for every push?

What happens: Each commit on a PR shows two identical runs.

Why: on: [push, pull_request] without filters triggers once for the push to the branch and once for the pull request.

What you do: Use the pattern from this chapter: push only for main, pull_request for everything else.

What if… a command fails, but the step is green?

What happens: You write run: uv run pytest | tee pytest.log to keep a log file. Tests fail, but the step and the job are green.

cards.s: Five more things you need in almost every workflow
cards.html:
Why: A shell pipeline's exit code is that of the last command (tee, which succeeded). When you do not set shell:, GitHub runs steps with bash -e {0}: it stops on errors, but without pipefail. With an explicit shell: bash it uses bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail {0}, and the step fails as it should.

What you do: Set it once for the whole workflow:

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

The same trap exists in any script with pipes: start your shell scripts with set -euo pipefail.

cards.s: Push it and watch it run
cards.html:
terminal:

git add .github/workflows/ci.yml
git commit -m "ci: run tests on every push"
git push

Open your repository on GitHub, click the Actions tab and then the run. You see the job test and, inside, each step with its log. Steps are collapsible; the first one, Set up job, shows the runner image version, which is useful when something worked yesterday and fails today.

cards.s: A red run, and how to read it
cards.html:
Try it: Break it on purpose

In src/credit_api/gate.py, change if new[name] < floor: to if new[name] > floor:. Commit on a branch, push, and open a pull request. Within a minute the PR shows a red cross: CI / test (pull_request) Failing.

Click Details next to the failing check and expand the red step. Always read a CI log from the bottom up: the summary is at the end.

expected output:

FAILED tests/test_gate.py::test_gate_passes_for_good_model
FAILED tests/test_gate.py::test_main_returns_exit_code
==================== 2 failed, 29 passed in 1.9s ====================
Error: Process completed with exit code 1.

Then scroll up to the first failure:

expected output:

cards.s: A red run, and how to read it
cards.html:
tests/test_gate.py:11: in test_gate_passes_for_good_model
    assert gate.check(new, BASE, FLOORS, max_drop=0.03) == []
E   AssertionError: assert ['roc_auc=0.7...ow floor 0.4'] == []
E     Left contains 2 more items, first extra item:
E     'roc_auc=0.7900 below floor 0.7'

The message says a good model (AUC 0.79) was reported as "below floor 0.7", so the comparison is inverted. Reproduce locally with uv run pytest tests/test_gate.py, fix it, push again: the same PR re-runs automatically and turns green.

Watch out: Typical first-run failures

cards.s: A red run, and how to read it
cards.html: uv sync --locked fails with "The lockfile needs to be updated": you changed pyproject.toml but did not commit the new uv.lock. Run uv lock and commit. Tests that pass locally but fail in CI usually depend on something only your laptop has: a file that is not committed (check .gitignore), an environment variable, a timezone or an absolute path.

cards.s: A field guide to red runs
cards.html:
The last lines of a failed log usually identify the category at once. These are the ones you will meet most:

Last lines of the logCause and fix
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'credit_api'The package is not installed in the environment pytest runs in. With the src/ layout, run tests through uv run after uv sync; with plain pip, pip install -e ..
FileNotFoundError: … data/german_credit.csvThe file is in .gitignore or was never committed. git ls-files data/ shows what Git actually has.
ERROR: … no tests ran / exit code 5pytest found no tests: wrong folder, or files not named test_*.py. Exit code 5 fails the job, which is good.
Error: Process completed with exit code 137.The runner killed the process: out of memory. Train on a smaller sample in CI, or use a larger runner.
The job running on runner … has exceeded the maximum execution time of 10 minutes.Your timeout-minutes hit. Often a test waiting forever for a network service, or a prompt waiting for input (apt-get install without -y).

cards.s: A field guide to red runs
cards.html:
Last lines of the logCause and fix
Passes on re-run without changesA flaky test: randomness without a seed, timing (sleep), test order, or an external service. Fix it at once; a team that gets used to "just re-run" stops trusting red builds.

Try it: Read logs faster from the terminal

With the GitHub CLI: gh run list shows recent runs, gh run view --log-failed prints only the failed steps' logs, and gh run rerun --failed re-runs only the failed jobs. For more detail, re-run in the UI with Enable debug logging, which prints every internal step of the runner and of the actions.

A badge in the README shows the status of the last run on main. In the Actions tab, open the workflow, click … → Create status badge, or write it yourself:

README.md:

# credit-api

![CI](https://github.com/<you>/credit-api/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)

The badge is small, but recruiters and interviewers notice it: it shows at a glance that your portfolio project is tested automatically and currently green.

Exercise: A test for the schema

Add a parametrized test to tests/test_api.py that sends three invalid requests (negative credit_amount, duration of 200, a missing purpose) and asserts status 422 for each.

Exercise: Trigger on a schedule

Make the Level 1 workflow also run every night at 04:00 UTC and add a manual "Run workflow" button. (Hint: schedule and workflow_dispatch.)

Exercise: Find the order dependence

Add a test at the end of tests/test_api.py that sets df["age"] = 0 on the session fixture without copying it. Run the whole suite and then only tests/test_data.py. Which tests fail, and why only in one case? Fix the test.

Exercise: The pipe trap

Add a step run: uv run pytest | tee pytest.log and break a test. Confirm that the job stays green. Then add defaults: run: shell: bash and confirm that it turns red.

Checkpoint: you should now be able to…

• create a project with uv, commit uv.lock, run uv run pytest;
  • write tests with fixtures, parametrize and pytest.raises;
  • compare floats with pytest.approx, write fixtures with teardown, and explain why a test can fail only in the full suite;
  • write behavioural tests for a model (baseline, skew, leakage, stability);
  • debug a workflow that does not start, runs twice, or stays green although a command failed;
  • explain on, jobs, runs-on, steps, uses and run;
  • find the cause of a red run by reading the log bottom-up;
  • show the CI status with a README badge.
